Valley of Succoth
VAL-ee of SUK-oth
proper noun
Hebrew 'emeq Sukkoth, “the valley of booths,” from sukkah, a booth or tabernacle, so named because Jacob built booths there for his cattle (Gen 33:17); a trans-Jordan valley the LORD claims as His to divide.

📖 Biblical Definition

When the LORD would prove His right to the land, He did not argue; He apportioned it. “God hath spoken in his holiness; I will rejoice, I will divide Shechem, and mete out the valley of Succoth” (Psa 60:6). Succoth lay beyond Jordan, in the trans-Jordan lowland where Jacob once built booths for his cattle; and David, singing of the LORD’s conquests, hears God claim that far valley as His own to measure with the line. To mete out is the act of an owner, not a suitor. The whole land—Shechem on this side, Succoth on that—is the LORD’s, and He portions it to whom He will. Here is the doctrine of sovereign inheritance writ in geography: the earth is the LORD’s, and every allotment among the tribes, from Heshbon and Mahanaim outward (Josh 13:26), came not by conquest merely but by grant. As the mountains stand round about Jerusalem, so the LORD stands round about His people (Psa 125:2), holding both land and heir in His hand. What comfort for the saint, whose inheritance is not seized but given, sure because the Giver is sovereign. Yet the trans-Jordan booths were never the rest itself; they pointed on, for here we have no continuing city, but seek one to come (Heb 13:14). The valley of Succoth teaches us to receive our portion from His hand and to look beyond it to the abiding city.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A trans-Jordan valley of booths that the LORD claims as His to portion—“I will…mete out the valley of Succoth” (Psa 60:6); a witness to God’s sovereign ownership of the land and the inheritance He grants.

expand to see more

VALLEY OF SUCCOTH, a trans-Jordan vale of booths (Psa 60:6).

So named because Jacob built booths there for his cattle.

The LORD divides Shechem and metes out this valley as an owner.

A figure of God’s sovereign portioning of the inheritance.

The saint receives his portion from the hand that owns the earth.

📖 Key Scripture

Psa 60:6 — "God hath spoken in his holiness; I will rejoice, I will divide Shechem, and mete out the valley of Succoth."

Josh 13:26 — "And from Heshbon unto Ramathmizpeh, and Betonim; and from Mahanaim unto the border of Debir;"

Psa 125:2 — "As the mountains are round about Jerusalem, so the LORD is round about his people from henceforth even for ever."

Heb 13:14 — "For here have we no continuing city, but we seek one to come."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The valley of Succoth recovers the sovereign ownership of God over all the land and His right to grant the inheritance to whom He will.

expand to see more

The valley of Succoth stands as a plain confession that the land is the LORD’s. He divides Shechem and metes out this trans-Jordan vale as an owner measures his own field, and every tribe held its portion not by right of sword but by grant of God. The earth is the LORD’s, and He gives the inheritance to whom He will.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. A vale of booths beyond Jordan raises no modern quarrel. The principle to recover is the sovereign ownership of God over all the earth, and His free right to portion the inheritance. The saint’s estate is not seized but given, sure because the Giver is sovereign; and every earthly allotment points beyond itself to the abiding city He has prepared for His own.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From sukkah, a booth, tent, or tabernacle; Succoth is “booths.”

expand to see more

Sukkoth — booths, from sukkah, a temporary shelter.

Jacob built booths there and called the place Succoth (Gen 33:17).

The same root names the feast of tabernacles.

'emeq — a valley or vale, the deep lowland.

To mete out (madad) is to measure with a line, as an owner.

Usage

"The LORD said He would mete out the valley of Succoth."

"Succoth was named for the booths Jacob raised there."

"The whole land is the LORD’s to divide as He pleases."
